To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Au(I) and the Cu(I) dithiophosphine and the Cu(I)-diaryl phosphine complexes are active in the in vitro L1210 cell system.
The antitumor complex, [Au(dppe)]Cl, inhibits protein synthesis, and uncouples oxidative phosphorylation in L1210 leukemia cells.
Au(I) and related Cu(I) complexes are potent uncouplers of mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylations and that the effect on nucleotide levels is a direct consequence of this uncoupling.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the mechanism of action of antitumor gold(I) diphosphanes and their copper(I) analogues.
the development of novel metal complexes as anticancer drugs.
the design of novel antitumor complexes of the metals gold and copper, and the investigation of their mode of action.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the antitumor activity of the gold(I) complex [Au(dppee)]Cl is due to its inhibition of the oxidative metabolism of the tumor cell, and this is probably due to the inhibition of the mitochondrial electron transport chain. 1H and 13
the antitumor activity of [Au(dppe)]Cl and [Cu(dppe)]Cl in vivo is not due to a specific effect of these complexes on the cell's nucleotide metabolism.

the antitumor activity of [Au(dppe)(2)](+) is not due to a direct effect on DNA synthesis or the inhibition of protein synthesis, but is due to a general uncoupling of oxidative phosphorylation in the mitochondria.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have demonstrated the use of 1H and31P NMR spectroscopy in conjunction with HPLC analysis of perchloric extracts of cultured mouse L1210 leukemia cells to investigate the effect of gold and copper diphosphine complex on the cellular metabolism.
we were the first to show the effects of Au(I) diphos complexes on cell metabolism, using a combination of HPLC and NMR.

the antitumor complexes [Au(dppe)]+ and [Cu(Ph 2PCHCHPPh2)]+ cause a marked inhibition of mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylations and a marked inhibition of protein synthesis in L1210 leukemia cells, whereas the complex [Cu(PEt2(CH2)PCH2PPh 2)Cl] does not affect ATP synthesis and inhibits protein synthesis only at higher concentrations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Au(I) and its analogs are capable of modulating the metabolism of tumor cells.
Au(I) and related complexes are not cytotoxic by themselves.
the gold complex [Au(dppee)2]Cl is a potent inhibitor of nucleotide metabolism in L1210 leukemia cells.
